identity.title: SOFIA/HAWC+ Detection of a Gravitationally Lensed Starburst Galaxy at z = 1.03

paper_type_evidence.quote: IRAM-30 (1.2 mm), ALMA (1.28, 2.8 mm), and JVLA (7GHz) (cite: Messias2014).
We perform a 27-band multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution modeling (SED) including the new SOFIA/HAWC+ data to constrain the fractional AGN contribution to the total IR luminosity.

evidence.quote: This system consists of an edge-on foreground disk galaxy at $z$ = 0.218 and a nearly complete Einstein ring of an intrinsic ultra-luminous infrared galaxy at $z$ = 1.027.

question.value: Is the IR luminosity of the lensed starburst J1429-0028 powered by pure star formation or also an AGN, and how well can SED modeling constrain its stellar mass and star formation history?

evidence.quote: Is this high IR luminosity powered by pure star formation (SF) or also an active galactic nucleus (AGN)?
We extracted the photometry of the source using an 1-FWHM radius aperture and the resultant flux density is 748.4 $\pm$ 101.1 mJy.

other_facilities.name: Herschel, SDSS, VIKING, HST, Spitzer, WISE, IRAM-30, JVLA

provided.value: Ancillary photometry from UV to radio

evidence.quote: Multi-wavelength photometry from rest-frame UV to radio has been obtained from SDSS ($u$, $g$, $r$, $i$, $z$), VIKING (Z, Y, J, H, K$_s$), *HST* (F110W)

what.value: De-blended, magnification-corrected photometry including ALMA 1.28 and 2.8 mm fluxes, and lensing magnification 9.7 +/- 0.7

evidence.quote: Using a lensing magnification factor of 9.7 $\pm$ 0.7 (cite: Messias2014)
We use the de-blended magnification-corrected photometry for the source to perform SED modeling.

what.value: ALMA photometry and source/lens de-blending taken from earlier work

evidence.quote: The de-blending of the foreground lens and background source is discussed in detail in (cite: Messias2014).

unstated_but_needed: ALMA observation details (bands, configurations, calibration, imaging) are not given
ALMA project code not printed in the paper
cigale and sed3fit parameter grids beyond those listed

method.value: CRUSH reduction, 1-FWHM radius aperture photometry, de-magnified by lens magnification

evidence.quote: the de-magnified flux density at 89 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ is 77.2 $\pm$ 11.8 mJy.

validation.value: Lens galaxy contribution estimated at most 3%

evidence.quote: The minor contribution to the observed flux density from the foreground lensing galaxy is estimated to be at most 3%, which is within the quoted uncertainties.

analysis_steps.goal: Panchromatic SED fitting with AGN and radio components

method.value: Energy-balance Bayesian SED fitting with sed3fit and cigale, varying SFH, attenuation and dust emission models one at a time

evidence.quote: Both cigale and sed3fit fit galaxy SEDs using a Bayesian approach to generate the posterior probability distribution function (PDF) for each parameter of interest

key_parameters.value: Chabrier IMF, BC03 stellar populations; double-tau SFH burst fraction free (0-1) or <=0.1

evidence.quote: ($f_{\rm burst}$ $\leq$ 0.1)

assumptions.value: Radio q Gaussian prior mean 2.34, sigma 0.25 in sed3fit

evidence.quote: A Gaussian prior distribution is assumed for the coefficient, $q$, with the mean at 2.34

fitting.value: Posterior PDFs; cigale weighted mean and std, sed3fit 16/50/84%

evidence.quote: sed3fit outputs the 16%, 50% (median), 84% values of the PDFs.

validation.value: Compared codes and models; tested cigale burst fraction recovery on merger simulations

evidence.quote: Likewise, we test cigale using merger simulations to check whether the burst fraction can be reasonably recovered.
The raw data was processed through the CRUSH pipeline v2.34-4 (cite: Kovacs2008)
the Code Investigating GALaxy Emission (cigale version v0.11; (cite: Noll2009; Roehlly2014))
we employ two SED fitting codes, sed3fit (cite: Berta2013)
which did not include AGN templates nor radio emission
the resultant flux density is 748.4 $\pm$ 101.1 mJy
the de-magnified flux density at 89 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ is 77.2 $\pm$ 11.8 mJy.

results_numeric.quantity: AGN IR fraction 3 sigma upper limit

evidence.quote: 3 $\sigma$ upper limit $f^{\rm AGN}_{\rm IR}$ $<$ 0.72%

findings_qualitative.value: Dust luminosity is the best constrained parameter and is consistent across models, >4e12 Lsun

evidence.quote: The dust luminosity is the best constrained parameter with least uncertainty

claims.hypothesis: An energetically important AGN contributes to the IR luminosity
claims.experiment: SED fits with AGN templates in sed3fit and cigale

evidence.quote: A significant AGN contribution to the IR luminosity has been ruled out at a high confidence level regardless of model choices.

claims.hypothesis: Stellar mass is robust given extensive photometry
claims.result: Stellar mass varies by up to a factor of about 10 depending on SFH
claims.finding: SFH dominates the stellar mass uncertainty

evidence.quote: We stress that star formation history is the dominant source of uncertainty in the derived stellar mass (as high as a factor of $\sim$ 10)

limitations_admitted.value: Blue end of the sed3fit SED is dominated by a spurious AGN component because of upper limits, so SED alone cannot indicate AGN

evidence.quote: We cannot rely on the SED fitting alone to infer AGN activity in this case

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA data are only reused photometry
Model grids are only partly described
Burst-fraction test with merger simulations is not detailed

reproducibility.score_reason: Photometry table is given and the codes are public, but grids and HAWC+ details are incomplete.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA data are not directly processed; the SED fits depend on unspecified parameter grids.
